about.title: About Tenantkit
about.lead: Tenantkit helps renters who don't have a lawyer meet their deadlines and send the right letter.
about.why1: Only about 3% of tenants have a lawyer in eviction cases, compared with 81% of landlords. Many renters miss a short deadline or never send the letter that would protect them.
about.why2: Free tools work when they exist, but most are built for one city or one state. Tenantkit is a reusable engine: each state's rules and letters are plain data files that legal aid groups and volunteers can add to.
about.how1: Every deadline and letter lives in a YAML file with links to the law it is based on. The app reads those files, counts days with each state's court holidays, and fills in letters from your answers.
about.how2: Each state says whether a licensed lawyer has reviewed its rules yet. Draft rules are written by volunteers from official sources and should be double-checked.
about.privacy1: There are no accounts, no analytics, no cookies and no ads. Letters and PDFs are made in your browser, and nothing you type is sent anywhere. The site's security settings block it from contacting any other server.
about.privacy2: If you choose “Remember my answers”, they are saved only in this browser until you clear them.
about.legal1: Tenantkit explains the law in plain language, but it can't know everything about your situation, and laws change. Use it as a starting point, and talk to a legal aid office or lawyer when you can, especially if you have court papers.
about.license1: The app's code is licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0, so it stays open, including when someone runs it as a website.
about.license2: The letters, rules and holiday calendars are licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0. Legal aid groups can copy and adapt them freely, as long as they give credit.
about.contribute1: Know your state's tenant law? You can add it without writing code. The content guide explains every file, and a checker tells you exactly what to fix.
